title: Chromatin Studio — build, inspect, and test a model
subtitle: An editable walkthrough of the actual application

delivery.timing_rule: Scene, keyframe and caption times are editable reference timings. The renderer scales each scene to its measured natural-paced neural narration plus a 1.25-second reading pause, rounded up to a video frame. Audio is never accelerated or truncated. Final timings are saved in render-timeline.json and render-manifest.json.
delivery.rendering_rule: Use actual application captures. A keyframe change represents the documented UI action. Pans and emphasis may help readability, but must not imply that a still image is a live trajectory. Do not fabricate events, data, bindings, RNA molecules, or successful cluster execution.
delivery.narration_engine: Local Kokoro-82M v1.0; af_heart voice; target 155 words per minute

scenes.title: Start with the workbench
scenes.narration: Chromatin Studio connects a model builder, a spatial simulation, and measurements from the current run. The starting example spans twenty megabases using two thousand beads, so each bead represents ten kilobases. That is a coarse genomic mapping, not nucleosome resolution. The center shows the applied model. Builder changes belong to the draft until they are applied. Begin by checking the scale, the run status, and the physical-clock label.

captions.text: Build on the left. Inspect the applied model in the center. Follow measurements and events.
20 Mb example = 2,000 beads × 10 kb. Individual nucleosomes are unresolved at this scale.
Draft settings and the current run are different. Check the scale and calibration status first.

scenes.title: Choose a focused experiment
scenes.narration: For the detailed walkthrough, choose Manuscript hypotheses at eighty kilobases. Four hundred coarse units represent two hundred base pairs each, with nucleosome occupancy and individual transcripts enabled. The preset includes transcription factors, coactivators, and illustrative active and repressive marks. These are starting hypotheses, not fitted biology. Expand builder gives the settings room. Ordinary edits stay in the draft until Apply and restart. How it works is a separate learning sandbox: its sliders explain equations without changing your run.

400 beads × 200 bp: coarse nucleosome units, without wrapped-DNA or histone-tail geometry.
“How it works” is a separate learning sandbox. Its controls leave the simulation unchanged.

scenes.title: Set the confining domain
scenes.narration: The polymer already has confinement. System now makes the wall explicit: outside the chosen radius, a harmonic force pushes particles inward. Increasing wall stiffness reduces penetration; zero switches the force off. This is a soft wall, so particles are not clipped back to the boundary. The diagnostics report excursions for mechanical particles and released RNA. For a small locus, this sphere is a modeled domain, not automatically an entire nucleus. Compare radius and wall strength, because packing can change contacts and transcription even when every biochemical parameter stays the same.

captions.text: The soft wall pushes inward outside R: U = ½k max(r − R, 0)².
Wall strength 0 disables confinement. Small penetrations are allowed and reported.
The modeled domain is not automatically the whole nucleus. Control packing and wall effects.

actions: Open System and show radius and wall strength.

scenes.title: Watch binding along the chromosome
scenes.narration: For a clear binding example, choose the twenty-five point six kilobase nucleosome-access preset. Open the one-dimensional genome and choose Live binding. Genes, nucleosome occupancy and directly bound proteins share one genomic axis. Navigate to a gene, then use Binding detail to see individual sites. Here, two hundred base pairs per bead represents a coarse nucleosome unit. In the twenty-megabase example, each symbol instead represents a much larger bin. Each molecule marker comes from a real chromatin bond; proximity alone is not binding. Run to watch bindings change, then pause and select a site. The table separates association and release hazards for each species. Times remain reduced until an empirical physical mapping is attached. All tracks restores the wider view of marks, loops, polymerases and protein preferences.

captions.text: Choose the 25.6 kb nucleosome-access example, then Live binding. Use Binding detail to inspect individual sites.
200 bp beads show coarse nucleosome units; 10 kb beads show effective bins. Proximity alone is not binding.
Select a site to compare association and release hazards. Times remain reduced unless a physical mapping is attached.

accuracy_notes: Only label occupancy as measured when the mechanism is enabled. Zoomed-out summaries aggregate beads or molecule counts.
A nucleosome symbol represents occupancy at a genomic site, not a persistent histone identity or resolved wrapped DNA.
Protein glyphs represent actual direct molecule–chromatin attachments; multiple IDR domains do not become multiple molecules.
Capture hazards are not equilibrium Kd or macroscopic molar kon. Site release hazards use the current occupancy state.
This video uses paused captures from genuine engine runs; the app itself updates the view while running.

This chapter explicitly changes the recording preset from the preceding 80 kb example. The following remodeler chapter uses this same 25.6 kb example.

scenes.title: Create gaps and recruit remodelers
scenes.narration: Stay in the nucleosome-access example. In Chromatin, define an initially vacant interval to create a nucleosome-free region. This sets the starting state; reassembly can fill the gap later. In Proteins, each species has separate occupied and vacant capture and release multipliers. Opening a site can favor one species and disfavor another, especially when eviction also removes a mark. Add chromatin remodeler creates an editable species and enables occupancy in the draft. Its eviction, reassembly and sliding rates act when it is attached to chromatin or recruited through a configured transcription factor. Eviction clears marks. Reassembly starts unmarked. Sliding moves occupancy and its marks into an adjacent vacant bead, conserving nucleosome number. Inspect Recorded binding and remodeling events to follow what actually occurred. These are recent recorded events, not a complete microscopic history. Apply changes only when ready to start a new run.

captions.text: An initially vacant interval creates a starting gap. Reassembly and remodeling can change it later.
Set occupied/vacant capture and release independently for each species. A gap need not favor every protein.
Eviction clears marks; reassembly starts unmarked; sliding moves occupancy and marks to an adjacent vacant bead.
Inspect actual recorded events. Sliding conserves nucleosome number; the recent event buffer is not a full trajectory.

accuracy_notes: The 25.6 kb example is illustrative and uncalibrated; all rates and event times are reduced units unless a valid physical mapping is attached.
Sliding is an adjacent-bead relocation of binary occupancy and marks, not base-pair-resolved remodeling or DNA unwrapping.
Remodelers use prescribed kinetic rates; there is no ATP, explicit histone reservoir, remodeler mechanochemical cycle or persistent histone identity.
Occupancy-sensitive release changes chromatin bond hazards at reaction updates. It does not force immediate release on eviction or change protein–protein off-rates.

Binding and release records come from actual engine transitions. Turnover records report interval endpoint changes and mark-reset intervals; they do not enumerate every hidden turnover within an interval.
The recent event buffer is bounded; absence from the retained list is not evidence that a transition never occurred.
Initial occupancy intervals and editor changes remain draft settings until Apply and restart.
Binding/release/sliding carry sampled conditional times; turnover records carry interval endpoints. Event IDs order emitted observations, not a globally interleaved exact reaction timeline.

scenes.title: Define many proteins and their roles
scenes.narration: Return to the eighty-kilobase manuscript example for the rest of the walkthrough. The Proteins editor defines each species independently. Expand builder gives these settings room. Set abundance, free diffusion, binding valence, mark preferences, and occupied-versus-vacant capture and release factors. A species can also write or erase a mark, or remodel nucleosomes. An IDR representation expands a molecule into a flexible chain of domain beads with binding stickers. This supports higher-order assemblies, but it is not an amino-acid-resolved protein model. Choose roles and interactions as explicit hypotheses; a biological name is not a calibrated parameter set.

captions.text: Use “Expand builder” to inspect each species’ abundance, free mobility, valence and chromatin preferences.
Writer, eraser and remodeling settings connect protein binding to chromatin-state changes.
IDRs are coarse domain-and-sticker chains. Biological names do not imply fitted molecular parameters.

scenes.title: Inspect binding in its context
scenes.narration: The interaction view shows the current molecular network. Distinguish molecules with their own chromatin bond from those tethered indirectly through another protein. Protein pairs can bind while both are free, while one is directly chromatin-bound, or while both are bound. The affinity calculator explores an ideal diffusion-limited association estimate after physical scales are supplied. Its nominal dissociation rate follows the requested Kd under independent, well-mixed assumptions. It does not turn the simulator's local encounter hazard into a measured molar association rate.

captions.text: Inspect free, directly bound and indirectly tethered molecules in the current binding network.
Higher-order assemblies can contain free–free, bound–free and bound–bound protein contacts.
The Kd calculator is an ideal physical estimate. It does not calibrate multivalent avidity or microscopic hazards.

scenes.title: Connect accessibility, marks and stiffness
scenes.narration: Nucleosome occupancy is an explicit local state when this option is enabled. Eviction can expose a TF site, clears marks at that site, and changes the configured local persistence multiplier. Bound writers and recruited coactivators can alter marks; spreading follows three-dimensional chromatin contacts. Mark-dependent chromatin attraction is a separate interaction from a protein's mark preference. The learning example lets you compare occupied and vacant capture hazards and persistence values. Those numerical relationships explain a hypothesis; the illustration is not an equilibrium polymer calculation.

captions.text: Nucleosome eviction can alter TF access and local stiffness, while clearing local histone marks.
Protein mark preferences and chromatin–chromatin attraction are separate model mechanisms.
Compare occupied and vacant states in the guide, then inspect the corresponding applied-model tracks.

accuracy_notes: At coarse 10 kb resolution this is an effective bin state; the recording preset instead uses coarse 200 bp nucleosome units.

scenes.title: Follow an enhancer to its target gene
scenes.narration: Regulation now shows the causal pathway for each gene. A transcription factor binds its configured region, and a coactivator is recruited through an actual protein bond. Enhancer contact can add to the target promoter's activation and initiation rates. The rate breakdown separates the baseline, recruitment, local mark gate and optional body response. Nucleosome occupancy changes transcription factor access; recruited enzymes can alter marks and accessibility. Basal activation can remain possible without recruitment. Losing contact removes its gain, but does not instantly turn an active promoter off or erase its chromatin memory.

captions.text: Define an enhancer’s interval, TF, coactivator and target gene in the Regulation builder.
Follow the causal map: recruitment × environment × mark gate determine effective activation.
Transcription is stochastic. Losing contact removes a rate gain; it does not instantly switch an ON promoter OFF.

accuracy_notes: Required/repressive marks at the gene start gate activation, not initiation by an already ON promoter.
TF region preferences are prescribed affinity multipliers, not sequence-motif scanning.
TF recruitment is a multiplicative gain above a basal factor of one, not a strict requirement for all transcription.

scenes.title: Watch polymerases produce individual RNA
scenes.narration: Transcription is stochastic. The engine now follows promoter switches within each reaction interval, and draws initiations only during the time actually spent active. Each new polymerase moves for the time remaining after its birth. Inspect its identity, position and growing RNA length in Elongation. Nucleosomes can slow movement; configured pauses have stochastic waiting times. Completed transcripts become diffusing points that can be processed or degraded. Nascent RNA can remain after a promoter switches off, so a nascent-positive gene is not the same as an active promoter.

captions.text: Initiations use actual time spent ON. New polymerases elongate only after their birth.
Advance real simulation time, pause, then select a molecule to inspect its identity and progress.
Promoter ON, nascent-positive, released and processed RNA are distinct observables.

scenes.title: Separate loops, assemblies and nuclear bodies
scenes.narration: Cohesin, protein assemblies and nuclear bodies organize space through different rules. Cohesin changes contacts through moving loop anchors. Protein bonds form higher-order assemblies. Speckles and the nucleolus are currently imposed fields, not self-generated condensates. In Genes, optional body responses can promote or suppress activation and initiation. A multiplier of one is neutral; the effect fades with promoter distance. These prescribed responses do not bypass the mark gate. Keep them separate from mechanical body attraction and from the speckle's effect on released RNA processing.

captions.text: Cohesin moves tethered anchors along chromatin; protein assemblies emerge from finite-valence bonds.
Speckles and nucleolus are imposed affinity fields. Their size and position are prescribed.
Body responses, mechanical affinity and RNA processing are separate hypotheses; multiplier 1 is neutral.

scenes.title: Give the polymer a defensible physical clock
scenes.narration: Calibrate can import a condition-specific Hansen reference. Then supply a matched, equilibrated simulation and independent length evidence. Importing data does not complete calibration. Match the observable, dimension, drift treatment and fitting window. Next, load the synthetic example to practice fitting. Inspect its overlay, residuals and slopes; it cannot be applied as experimental evidence. A shared polymer clock converts reduced durations and rates consistently, but does not independently fit protein diffusion, binding residence times, elongation or Kd. Compatible empirical mappings retain their sources and baseline model fingerprint.

captions.text: Import a condition-specific Hansen reference. A matched equilibrated simulation and independent length evidence are still required.
Practice with the synthetic fit: inspect the overlay, residuals and slopes. Synthetic results remain demonstrations.
A shared clock converts units, not every biological parameter. Empirical mappings retain sources and a baseline-model fingerprint.

scenes.title: Ask what the model actually reproduces
scenes.narration: The benchmark panel separates implementation checks, an ideal Rouse reference, and published-figure replication. Solid curves show sampled reference trajectories; dashed curves show analytical predictions. The saved suite tests free diffusion, internal-chain motion, center-of-mass diffusion and illustrative static-loop suppression. These fixtures exercise the actual Brownian integrator but bypass the production forces and coupled reaction system. Passing them is evidence about implementation. It is not a reproduction of every figure in the cited paper, and it supplies no experimental clock.

captions.text: Compare sampled reference trajectories with analytical curves, then inspect the saved checks and provenance.
Gaussian-chain reference fixtures test the Brownian integrator, not every production-model coupling.
Implementation agreement, empirical calibration and published-figure replication are separate achievements.

accuracy_notes: Refresh pass counts from the saved report when rebuilding the video; do not hard-code a historical count into narration.
Internal polymer curves remove center-of-mass translation; separate COM checks test whole-chain motion.

scenes.title: Separate competition and shared environments
scenes.narration: Studies provides a simpler model for the manuscript's cis and trans comparison. Each simulated cell has four promoters: two genes on each of two homologs. All four share cell-wide variation. Genes on the same homolog may compete or experience a common fluctuating environment. The reference has no spatial polymer. Start with independent promoters, then add competition or shared environments separately. The experiment runs in isolation, leaving your current simulation untouched. Its purpose is to test whether a mechanism can produce a pattern, before asking whether the full spatial model or the experimental data support it.

captions.text: Four promoters represent two homolog pairs within each cell.
Compare competition, homolog-specific environments and cell-wide variation separately.
Isolated study runs preserve the live simulation. The reference contains no spatial polymer.

scenes.title: Read correlations without confusing controls
scenes.narration: After the study finishes, compare cis and trans correlations and their difference. The interval reflects sampling uncertainty, not proof of causality. Switch between latent nascent activity, detected activity and promoter state; these observables answer different questions. The spatial pilot instead measures two genes on one chain across independent replicas. Its independent-replica null is not a trans-allele control. Download the plan and results to retain parameters, seeds and limitations. Reproducing the manuscript quantitatively still requires the underlying data, matched observation models, calibrated units and substantially longer converged experiments.

captions.text: Φcis and Φtrans share the same cells. ΔΦ = Φcis − Φtrans.
Nascent-positive ≠ promoter ON. Detection assumptions affect observed correlations.
The one-chain spatial pilot has no matched trans alleles; its replica null is labeled separately.

scenes.title: Export a reproducible cluster experiment
scenes.narration: When the model is ready, open Cluster job. Choose the device platform, independent replicas, output intervals and resource requests, then preview the scripts before exporting. The bundle carries the draft configuration, code, seeds and validation workflow for a fresh run. It does not resume the current live state. GPU integration is available, while forces, reactions and RNA still run on the CPU; speedup is not established. Keep the model, inputs and results together, and use controlled comparisons to turn a visual hypothesis into testable evidence.

captions.text: Configure independent replicas, platform, sampling intervals and resources. Preview before exporting.
A portable bundle starts fresh from the draft. GPU integration is partial; speedup still needs measurement.
Build → inspect → calibrate → test. Preserve seeds, model provenance and controlled comparisons.

update_workflow: Edit the relevant scene title, narration, captions or semantic actions in this JSON file.
Recapture only affected UI keyframes, preserving the stable filenames or updating their references here.
Review model claims against the current README and implementation. Refresh numerical benchmark evidence from its saved report.
